Resolves #20409

A Gallery can now finish mounting while its Store is empty without dereferencing a missing record. Its initial selection waits for a visible record, runs once, and then leaves later manual deselection alone. The normal populated choice is retained, single-row indices are clamped, and an existing business key `0` is preserved. Unmount, destruction and every window transition retire stale measurement and selection work.

Evidence: L3 (the real Gallery example holds its request open until the native dimension read finishes, then renders and selects arriving rows) → L3 required. No residual acceptance gates.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `component/GalleryMountSelection.spec.mjs` empty mount; `rendering/StoreLoadingNL.spec.mjs` holds data through the actual native-read boundary |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: late data consumes one request; a selected key waits through unrelated chunks for its record; disabled selection and later manual deselection survive further loads/sorts |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: normal populated choice, single-row/one-record bounds and an existing business key zero |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: deferred reply after unmount/destroy/window change, older remount and max-items re-entry replies, A→B→A window round trip, completed empty measurement followed by window change, owned timeout cancellation and genuine-error controls |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: real mount-hook unit cases, real Gallery sort fixture and held-request Gallery/Helix native cases |

## Deltas from ticket

The delayed native read is one awaited, terminally handled task. A private mount generation fences its completion; a private pending flag is consumed only after a valid choice. Window changes retire both before forwarding the inherited window hook.

The older sort-restoration test borrowed Gallery's method onto a plain object. It now uses a real Gallery and Store, retaining the concrete model, fresh-node annotation and camera-call assertions while exercising the new lifetime state.

The native loading test also chooses its click by settled browser hit-testing. Overlapping 3D cards can put a different record at the first DOM item's click point; worker selection must match the actual native target.

## Test Evidence

The original empty-mount unit case failed with the same `undefined[Symbol(Neo.internalId)]` error as the [hosted failure](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42132796824/job/127614322043).

The native spec waits for observed `offsetWidth` before releasing any rows, so it cannot pass merely because data wins the 300 ms race. It then checks one rendered selected Gallery item; the error fixture is unchanged. `StoreLoadingNL.spec.mjs` passed three consecutive Gallery/Helix repetitions with the explicit E2E config and an owned Brain Bridge (six cases). Each run retains its pending-row screenshot and trace.

Two rejected candidates are pinned by tests: consuming selection on the first nonempty chunk lost a preselected key arriving in the next chunk; window-ID equality alone admitted A→B→A stale replies. The native trace also falsified the old DOM-first click oracle: it requested record 4 but the browser hit record 1, which the worker correctly selected. The replacement waits for finite motion, excluding the deliberately running loading spinner, then asserts both DOM annotation and worker selection for the hit-tested record.

`agent-preflight` is not hosted in Engine; local hooks and the shared PR baseline provide its applicable checks. Change class: restoration.

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (non-blocking): A preselected key whose record never arrives keeps the request pending indefinitely. `#selectInitialItem` returns while `!me.store.get(selection[0])`, so a stale or deleted preselection means the default is never chosen.
